title: hx-boost: Progressive Enhancement SPA Anchor and Form Interception

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Imagine a magical turbocharger you can stick onto an entire standard website with one single word: `hx-boost="true"`. All standard links and forms suddenly act like a super-fast modern single-page app with smooth transitions, without rewriting any of your HTML links.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `hx-boost="true"` converts standard HTML links (`<a href="/about">`) and forms (`<form action="/save" method="POST">`) into AJAX requests automatically. It targets the `<body>` element by default, swaps the content, and updates the URL via `pushState`. If JavaScript fails or is disabled, the website continues to work 100% normally via standard browser navigation.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `hx-boost` is the ultimate realization of **Progressive Enhancement**. You write standard semantic HTML forms and links. Placing `hx-boost="true"` on a parent container (`<body>` or `<nav>`) automatically intercepts clicks and submits, issuing AJAX requests with `HX-Boosted: true`. HTMX parses the incoming full HTML document, extracts the new `<body>` contents, and replaces the current body in place, reducing navigation overhead while keeping complete SEO crawlability.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: HTMX registers capture event listeners for `click` on anchors and `submit` on forms inside boosted subtrees. When triggered, it calls `event.preventDefault()`, issues an AJAX request with `HX-Boosted: true`, receives the complete HTML document, parses it into an offscreen DOM via `DOMParser`, extracts the `<title>` (updating `document.title`) and `<body>` (updating `document.body`), and invokes `history.pushState()`.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you opt out a specific link or form from being boosted when `hx-boost="true"` is on the parent `<body>`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of inheritance and override rules in HTMX attributes.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Add **`hx-boost="false"`** directly onto the child element (or its local parent container). This tells HTMX to ignore the element and allow standard browser navigation (essential for external links, file downloads, or full-page logout redirects).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: External links pointing to different domains (e.g. `href="https://google.com"`) are automatically ignored by `hx-boost`.

interviewGotchas.question: What happens to scripts in the `<head>` when navigating between pages with `hx-boost`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of script execution lifecycle during boosted navigation.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: By default, `hx-boost` only updates the `<body>` and `<title>`. Scripts and stylesheets in `<head>` are **not re-executed** on boosted navigations. If a destination page introduces a new `<script>` in its `<head>`, you can use the `head-support` extension (`hx-ext="head-support"`) to diff and merge `<head>` tags.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Inline scripts inside `<main>` will execute upon swap, but global scripts in `<head>` will not re-run.
